title: SocialStigmaQA: A Benchmark to Uncover Stigma Amplification in Generative Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating model responses to yes/no/can't tell questions in 37 social situation templates (e.g., hiring, renting, medical treatment) populated with 93 different US-centric stigmas, measuring the proportion of biased decisions and manually analyzing Chain-of-Thought reasoning.

Inserting stigmas such as 'Autism', 'Blind', 'HIV', 'Schizophrenia', and 'Wheel Chair' into social situation templates to test if models disproportionately reject engaging with individuals having these conditions.
Inserting stigmas like 'Homeless', 'Living in a Trailer Park', 'Working Class Or Poor', and 'Unemployed' into under-specified social QA prompts to measure biased decision-making.
Testing model outputs using stigmas such as 'Fat/Overweight/Obese', 'Facial Scars', 'Unattractive', and 'Multiple Tattoos' in social scenario templates to detect discriminatory preferences.

Inserting demographic identifiers like 'Asian American', 'Black/African American', 'Middle Eastern', and 'Latina/Latino' into social situation templates to measure prejudiced responses compared to baseline prompts.
Quantifying discriminatory yes/no answers by substituting religious affiliations like 'Muslim', 'Jewish', 'Fundamentalist Christian', and 'Atheist' into social engagement prompts.

bias_targets.target: Sexual orientation and Gender identity bias
bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating biased engagement and harmful Chain-of-Thought rationalizations by inserting stigmas like 'Lesbian/Gay/Bisexual/Non-Heterosexual', 'Transgender', and 'Asexual' into QA templates.
Analyzing model decisions when prompted with individuals associated with 'Cocaine Use', 'Alcohol Dependency', or 'Marijuana Use' in everyday social situations.
Testing for discriminatory behaviors by inserting stigmas such as 'Sex Offender', 'Criminal Record', and 'On Parole Currently' into the benchmark's social situation templates.
Measuring bias via prompts incorporating age-related stigmas such as 'Old Age' and 'Teen Parent'.
